learning_outcomes.statement: After Chapter 3 the learner can create and run a .py file, use the Python REPL and print()/input(), and correctly read SyntaxError/NameError/IndentationError tracebacks.
The learner can explain names as references to objects rather than boxes, predict rebinding behavior, and distinguish script/REPL/notebook/IDE and terminal/shell/Python-REPL.

reviewers.attestation: Read scripts/build_chapter_003.py in full (all lesson-builder functions), cross-checked every printed/claimed code result by executing the corresponding snippets under the project's own .venv (Python 3.14.6), verified two external claims (PEP 773 Windows installer timeline; pysh-shell.com/PyPI pysh-shell authenticity) via web search, and confirmed the canonical source sha256 matches the frozen M01 baseline exactly (no drift since baseline).

criteria.rationale: Every factual claim was checked: CPython's compile-to-bytecode-then-execute model, __pycache__ behavior, refcounting bounded correctly as a CPython detail (not a language guarantee, with PyPy noted as a counterexample), and the REPL Read-Eval-Print-Loop mechanics all read as correct on full inspection.

REPL banner text, traceback wording ('was never closed' for unterminated parens, current-style caret markers) and name/rebinding semantics were reproduced exactly under a real Python 3.14.6 interpreter with no discrepancy from the chapter's claims.

The chapter carefully separates 'shell' (OS command interpreter) from 'Python Shell/REPL' (a common English-documentation collision) with an explicit warning callout, and consistently uses 'ссылка' (reference) rather than 'переменная содержит значение' for the name-binding model established in Chapter 3.

The opener promises file execution, terminal/shell/REPL, the shell family, PySH, REPL tools, print()/input(), names, comments, IDLE, tracebacks, debugging, notebook/kernel and a mini-project; full reading confirms all 17 promised topics are delivered with working examples.

The one third-party tool claim in the chapter (PySH: real project, real PyPI package, real license/version framing) is independently confirmed via the project's own site and PyPI listing rather than taken on faith.
Section 3.17's summary_box states observable outcomes (distinguish terminal/shell/REPL, use print()/input(), read three named exception types, use a debugger) rather than a vague topic list.

The chapter explicitly defers int()/type conversion detail to Chapter 4 and only uses concepts already established in Chapter 1-2 (interpreter, PATH) or introduced earlier in this same chapter before relying on them (e.g. names before NameError, print before input).

3.1 motivates the file/interpreter model with a cooking-recipe analogy before any syntax; 3.9's name-vs-box discussion opens with the misconception directly before the correct model, which is the recommended predict-explain sequence.

The refcounting/cyclic-GC deep dive is explicitly marked optional ('можно спокойно пропустить') and chunked as a clearly delimited aside, preventing it from raising cognitive load for the core lesson.
3.17 closes with a genuine mini-project (terminal business-card program) that requires composing input()/print()/naming from the whole chapter, plus a full retrieval-style summary_box.
The name/reference/rebinding terminology introduced here is reused identically and extended (not contradicted) in Chapter 4's number-object sections, confirmed during the same batch read.
Internal references to Chapter 2 (PATH, sys.executable, venv) and forward references to later chapters (lists, functions) are accurate and appropriately hedged ('мы вернёмся позже').

The terminal/shell/REPL distinction is deliberately restated at increasing precision across 3.2, 3.3 and 3.6 rather than duplicated verbatim, each time adding new information (shell family, then REPL-as-tool).
All 17 section identifiers, the sidebar practice list (03-01..03-10), and PAGES ordering are internally consistent with no ID collision or mismatched title.

evidence.summary: pysh-shell.com and PyPI confirm PySH ('PySH — Python Automation Platform', package pysh-shell, pip install pysh-shell) is a real, currently maintained project matching the chapter's description and installation instructions, not a fabricated tool.

All 18 ChapterSectionLink entries in build_opener() resolve to real lesson-builder functions with matching headings; the 10 practice_card() references (03-01..03-10) map one-to-one onto the 10 notebooks in notebooks/chapter-03/ with no gap or duplicate.

The PySH 'real session' code_block in 03-08-pysh.html embeds the actual development machine's username (astra), hostname (soi), and a git branch name (feat/curriculum-v2-chapter-03) as part of demonstrating unfabricated output. This is not factually wrong and is explicitly justified in-page as an authenticity measure, but is noted here as a suggestion-level observation for the human release gate: an author may want to decide deliberately whether personal machine identifiers belong in publicly shipped course material, rather than have that decision made silently by a future edit. Not scored against any chapter_opener criterion because the content lives in a theory_lesson (03-08), not in this opener unit; recorded here for traceability and carried into the batch narrative report as F-001 (suggestion, not fixed).
